utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Flynn, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Colonel Gerritsen, before the -- before the break you had told us about your meeting with Colonel Siljeg on the 19th of August and your visit with the Muslim POWs in the technical school in Prozor, and you expressed your concerns to Colonel Siljeg when you found out about the fact that they had been used as forced labour on the front line. Did the position improve? Did you get any information to suggest that this was no longer the position, that prisoners were no longer being used on the front line as heretofore, or did it still continue?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: It did continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And moving on, in your ICTY statement, at the foot of page 10, you make reference again to -- to sighting Muslim POWs being used by the HVO to dig trenches. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: This was on the 26th of August. If you could turn to Exhibit 9634. Again, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, daily report, 26th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And you're one of the authors of the document?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I'm one the authors with Hauenstein.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And turn to paragraph 4. In your note there under Humanitarian Activity where you say "V2 observed again HVO in Trnovaca using 25 POWs/civilian internees to dig trenches in the area of the front line." Is this what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's what I'm referring to, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And it's also noted in your report that, "V2 has made strong protests to the HVO in Prozor on this matter to no avail."

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: So you were getting no response from the HVO?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And how often would you -- would you raise this issue with the HVO authorities?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I think these kind of issues, also humanitarian, each time we met each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Can you tell us did you try through other means to influence the HVO to stop the use of forced labour on the battlefield?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No. The own mean we have is our daily report, which was sent by Travnik, Zenica, to Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Could I ask you to turn to Exhibit 4549.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: At the top of the page it says from V2 Gornji Vakuf, daily report, 27th of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did you assist in preparing it?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And again go -- go to the paragraph 4 under Humanitarian Activity, item A. You see it says -- you'll see under humanitarian activity it says the church in Prozor have taken on four projects within their area of prompt. "A. Conditions (including putting pressure on the HVO to stop using prisoners to dig trenches on the front line) ..." Did you enlist or did you try to enlist the assistance of the church or how did this notation arrive in your report?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Well, we spoke to the priests in Prozor on a regular basis, and we also discussed the same subjects as the priest as the major -- as with the military commander in Prozor. So this is correct and not -- not -- not strange.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And did you get any feedback from the church in Prozor as to whether or not they had any -- had any positive response from the HVO?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No, not that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Could we then skip to September --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Could I --

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Flynn, as we have the document in front us. In the same paragraph, 4, D -- in D we find: "Exchange of minorities between Prozor and Bugojno ..." Could you tell the Chamber what this refers to? Is this a programme of population exchange?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that -- that's -- you're right, difficulty this subject is, because we are not allowed to -- we are not propose to allow ethnical cleansing, and this could be a kind of ethnical cleansing when you exchange minorities, because here is meant the minority in Bugojno, which was Croat minority, and in Prozor was Muslim minority. And as far -- at this time I say it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: But would --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With our help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: But what you're saying is -- here is that this is a programme which was carried through by the church in Prozor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a second, please. Colonel, a follow-up question. You mentioned a Muslim minority of Prozor. I believe there must have been an imam in Prozor. The Catholic church had a role to play that is very honourable. They had four projects and that was very honourable, of course, but why did you not go to see the imam in order to try to coordinate the religious action on both sides?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We visited the imam in Prozor as much as possible. We were not always allowed to go to the imam, and we also discussed with him the same matters as we did with the priest in Prozor, and most of the times the same subjects. The -- we were not allowed to talk with the imam on several occasions by the military police of Prozor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, sir, why did you not state in your report that you had also met the imam and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These reports are written on a daily basis, and when we didn't met the imam that day, we didn't mention it in -- we didn't mention it in our daily report that we didn't met the imam. We only mentioned the people we have met. So on the 27th of August -- 27th of August, we didn't met the imam of Prozor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much. Please proceed, Mr. Flynn.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And staying with this subject of forced labour, could I skip forward to the -- to the 9th of September, 1993. Do you remember, did you or your colleague have occasion to visit the POW detention facility in programme on that date?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: On the 9th of September?

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I have not a date -- exactly the date in my memory. I should have --

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: If we can --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: -- a look at the daily report.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: If we can turn to Exhibit 9661, please.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: This is the daily report of the 9th of September. And we have visited that day the POW camp at Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And in the body of the report it says: "The camp is not a military detention camp but a detention camp for civilian internees."

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Why was there a need to hold civilian internees?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I do not know. They just did on both sides, and it could be a reaction of what all happened in Bugojno. It's a possibility. Maybe there were threats. The real reason we never heard. The only reason when we heard of that was that it was for their own security.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And you report mentioned there were 228 civilians imprisoned -- imprisoned in the camp. When you say "imprisoned in the camp," do I take it from that they did not have freedom of movement?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And it goes to say that almost every day they're digging trenches in the area of Trnovaca. The next sentence, and I'm not sure there's something missing from it: "At least four detainees during the digging." Do you know what was meant to be said there? It doesn't exactly make sense as drafted.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: For the digging. Which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: The same paragraph we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Paragraph 4, around six is lines down where it says: "They are digging trenches in the area of Trnovaca." You say, "At least four detainees have during digging." Do you recollect what was meant to be said there?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I still can't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Okay. If you turn to paragraph 4?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: 4, six --

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Paragraph 4 and go down one, two, three four five --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Slashes? No --

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Go down six sentences.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Oh, yes. No. That's not the correct sentence. I see, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Do you know what was meant to be said there?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No, I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And the paragraph goes on and it says: "In the absence of the camps guards the internees mentioned that they thought between 40 to 60 people had been killed working on the trenches." Now, was this complaint different to the complaint that you received earlier on the 19th of August?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And were you -- were you able in any way to confirm what you were told?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No. The only confirmation we had was what we saw -- we saw on several occasions people digging trenches, but we couldn't speak to those people who were digging trenches at that specific moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did you get a list at any stage of those people who were alleged to have been killed?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No. Although we've got several lists in my stay, overall stay, in the area of Gornji Vakuf, and we passed all this -- most of them to ICRC and to RC Zenica, but I do not remember a specific list for those people who died during digging trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: So you weren't able to make any independent inquiries because you didn't have names.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's correct, but these kind of inquiries we didn't make at all. We just asked questions and --

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Okay. So you're saying it didn't fall within your mandate?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, looking at your ICTY statement again and turning to page 12, I see that on the 13th of September you report that you had seen civilians in civilian clothes digging trenches, guarded by the HVO. Do you remember stating that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And if we could turn to the Exhibit 9629. Again it's a daily report.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: The 13th of September, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: The 13th of September. Again this is the daily report from Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, with MacIver.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: MacIver. By this stage had you received a new colleague?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And his name was Mr. MacIver?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: A Canadian, I believe?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: A Canadian, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And if we look the -- the statement in the -- if you look at your report under paragraph 3, Military Activity, you state, "In our AOR the preparations for future action are continuing. Again today, the V2 observed civilian labour digging trenches in forward HVO positions." Can you remember where it was that you saw the -- the civilian labour digging the trenches?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No. We saw it on several locations and most of the time we saw the neighbourhood of Makljen check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And were you able to approach the prisoners on this occasion to enquire under the circumstances they were forced to work, how many of them, who they were, et cetera, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Because it is too dangerous to go into the field because of mines, and I think they would not be pleased when we walked just through these people. So you take a risk which we couldn't take.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, we've referred to a number of instances where either you received reports of people being used for forced labour or you witnessed it yourself, and you told us on a number of occasions that you made reports, you made complaints or you brought it to the attention of the HVO authorities. At any stage after either obtaining the information or receiving it yourself or lodging any kind of process, did you ever get a positive response back from the HVO?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: The positive response was that they would investigate sometimes, but we never got a result.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And by way of contrast, did you have similar issues with POWs on the ABiH side, Croat prisoners, that you had to raise with the ABiH authorities?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And what kind of a response did you receive from them?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Nothing positive.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Nothing positive.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down for the transcript, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now, given the apparent BiH success to the north and the movement of its army southwards, can you tell us how Muslims were being treated in the -- in the town of Prozor by Croat authorities? Did they have, for example, freedom of movement?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No, they had not, and I think over the time it was more or less deteriorating. At a certain moment they were gathered.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: After that, they were expelled to another region.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And can you tell us who was it who was looking after the interests of the Muslim population living in Prozor during the period of your tenure in -- in the AOR of Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Well, we took a look at that as Victor 2. Also, of course, the imam of Prozor. I think one way or another sometimes also the priest did their best. Well, that's mainly it, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And is it correct to say that in your ICTY statement that on the 10th of August, 1993, you spoke with the imam at Prozor -- in Prozor at his house. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I spoke on several occasions with the imam at Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And if we could turn Exhibit 9619.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: The 10th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: The 10th of August.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Daily report, Hauenstein Gerritsen, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: You say under the third paragraph the report states, second sentence: "Most of the Muslim population is under house arrest and V2 has been forbidden to talk to them. It is not clear how many Muslims still remain in this area. However, three weeks ago it was about 5.000." Is that correct what --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And where did you get this information that Muslim population was under house arrest?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: From the imam and also from other sources. We also visited at a certain moment Podgrad and we could see that house arrest by ourselves, and the imam was always under house arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: In fact, if we turn to page 2 of that report, under Humanitarian Activity paragraph 4, four subparagraphs down, is it correct when you write: "The imam in Prozor to whom we talked to for about five minutes before the local police stated all the Muslims in the area had been gathered in the eastern part of the town. In one case there is up to 60 Muslims living in one house. He himself was under house arrest and must report to the police station three times each day."

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Well, that's correct, and he has said 80 Muslims in one house, but okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And who as it that the -- the -- who was it specifically that the imam was having this difficulty with? Was it --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: It was the military police of Prozor. They were gathering -- not gathering, but -- to -- they got the imam.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And you state in your ICTY statement that the military police were not under the authority of -- of Colonel Siljeg. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Do you know under whose authority they were?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And what kind of a relationship did ECMM have with him?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: A bad relationship we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: We tried to communicate, but it was difficult to communicate with -- the people from the military police were rude to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: How would you describe the manner in which they carried out their job, their functions?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Well, I would say very badly. They are not the kind of police we know of and, well, it's just -- I'm searching for the right word, but that difficult -- but they are not kind people. Rough, harsh, not well-educated. That was our opinion. They -- there was always a type of woman in that house, kind of whorehouse, in our opinion. It was a strange setting.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: So you told us about the fact that you learned that the Muslims had been arrested, and the imam had told you that they had all been gathered in the eastern part of the town. Was this a new development or had you seen it happen before?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: This was in Prozor a new development, a new development for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Did it give you cause for any concern?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, of course, because being held in a ghetto from a historical point of view isn't always a -- well.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And did you try to get confirmation as to what the imam had told you, that these people had been gathered in one part of the town? Did you try to get independent confirmation?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes. We asked to visit these people, and later on we visited, as I said before, Podgrad and later on Duge.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: At this time did you have any relationship with the chairman of the humanitarian commission, and did you make any inquiries from them?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes. Once we met a representative of a humanitarian commission in Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And if you -- if you turn to Exhibit 9630.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: The 11th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: The 11th of August. Again, are we looking at the daily report for this date? "Subject: Daily report, 11th of August, 1993. From V2 Gornji Vakuf to CC Travnik." Is this the daily report for that date?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And paragraph 4, Humanitarian Activity, there's a notation that V2 met with the chairman of the humanitarian commission, and on paragraph 5 again it says -- sorry, the next page, it says: "She stated --" the V2 met with the chairman of the humanitarian commission in Prozor. She stated that food stocks have been arriving in Prozor without difficulty." Is that correct so far?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And later in the paragraph, "She also confirmed that the imam had stated what we had reported in yesterday's daily report." So she confirmed with you that these people had been moved; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And we see as we look farther down that the V2 was once again restricted from seeing the imam in Prozor, and you commented that, "We will bring this up again with local military authorities." Who did you normally bring it up with?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: With Colonel Siljeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Why did you feel that Colonel Siljeg could do anything if he had no authority, as you indicated in your ICTY report?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Well, because of the fact that he was the man to talk with on all subjects, and if you want to achieve something you could achieve it most likely by him. We also raised these kind of subjects with the mayor of Prozor and the priest.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: And the -- well, we -- we tried everything, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And in the last part of that report that you're just looking at, under Assessment you say: "Concern is expressed over the fate of the Muslims in Prozor." Now, up to this all you had known was they were moved to the eastern part of Prozor?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: What was concerning you?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Well, in this war we had all reasons to be concerned when people are gathered -- well, you could expect that from -- as I said before, from the history that it is not well for these people to be gathered. It's always for a reason, and we had the conviction that it was not for their own safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And did you protest, did you make any protest to the HVO authorities?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, we always did.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And if we turn to Exhibit 9631, we see on the 13th of August you visited with the HVO authorities. Again, are we looking at a daily report for that date?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: The 13th it of August, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Under paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: "V2 once again protested to Prozor authorities over the restriction of access to Muslim leaders in the community. They promised that this restriction will be lifted." Did you take the opportunity of discussing the issue of -- as to why the people had been moved to the east of Prozor on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: It's possible that we did that on that occasion. Well, we did it on several occasions, but was probably also on this occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And if you turn --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Is it not on the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Not on this one. If you turn to --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: If you turn to Exhibit 9627.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: 9627. The 16th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Yes. And on that day did you have a meeting with the mayor of Prozor?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Jozic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And did he tell you anything about the Muslims that had been moved? Under Political Situation, there is a notation that "V2 met with the mayor of Prozor --"

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: "-- and he stated that most of his efforts are directed to day to day crisis management. He said the biggest problem was dealing with the influx of detainees --"

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. I see. Well, he stated there that they are also being moved to get more places for the Croat refugees. Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Well, I guess also an argument. Probably it's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Well, if you read the paragraph, it's -- did you prepare this report?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I did. With Hauenstein, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And he says at the middle of paragraph 2: "They are trying to care for all, including Muslims." And he refers to 70 per cent Croats and 30 per cent Muslims. At this point, had there been a large influx of Croat DPs into Prozor? Displaced persons.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Okay. Displaced persons, yes. I'm not sure. There were of course displaced persons, but I do not know the exact influx.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Well, you conclude the paragraph by stating: "He," the mayor, "feels the greatest responsibility is the safety of all civilians in Prozor."

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Were you reassured by that comment? Were you --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: One way or not I think so, but it depends on the circumstances of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: When circumstances are deteriorating, the people, also the mayor, could have possibility to -- could have difficulties, I mean, to implement his wishes as he has expressed here. You are never sure in wartime. But I think overall he tried to do his best, Jozic. As far as I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Do you ever remember mentioning in your ICTY statement to the investigators that you didn't believe that the men were being kept for their own safety?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: But that you believed it was part -- part of an ethnic cleansing campaign of the Croats?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes. What -- the question is, was the mayor of whom we are talking now responsible for the ethnical cleansing.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: No, but my question to you was when he had indicated that he feels for the -- the greatest responsibility is the safety of all the citizens in Prozor, was this a genuine intention on his part to provide for all the safety -- for the safety of all the citizens of Prozor?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Well, I think he -- as a Croat he is more in favour in wartime for the Croats of course, but a certain concern for the Muslims he had as well, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. I'm looking again at this daily report of the 16th of August. You'll see at the bottom of the page there's a notation: "V2 was once again restricted from talking to the imam in Prozor. We will once again protest. However, the imam did manage to tell us that all Muslim men between the ages of 16 to 60 who remained in Prozor have been gathered up and taken away."

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: What did he mean by that, "taken away"?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That they were imprisoned or expelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did you know to where they had been taken?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Well, I think these are the same - I'm not sure - as the people who are detained in the Prozor POW camp. Or not. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise for interrupting. I do my best not to. But in the past two questions, one after another, my learned friend has asked the witness what the person he was talking to thought when making a certain statement. I think that's speculation. The witness told us what he talked to said and that's what he wrote in his statement. Now, what the person thought, I don't think there's any point in going into that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I noted your comment. Mr. Flynn.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: If we turn back, Colonel, to Exhibit 4307 for a moment, please. And this was the 19th of August, 1993, that you've already spoken about. And if you turn to page 2, we see the reference to the prisoners held in Prozor technical school whom you visited. And then in the next paragraph it stated: "We have also been informed that the Muslims in Prozor have been moved into three areas of the region: Podgrade, Lapsunj, and Duge." Can you tell us who gave you this information? From whom did you obtain it?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I think it was from the imam of Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And when he was referring to the Muslims in Prozor, was he referring to those Muslims who had earlier been moved into the eastern area?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, these are the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And if we continue on through that particular paragraph we're looking at, is it correct to state that you managed to visit one of those places on the date you got the information?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Later on we visited Podgrade and Duge. So two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And in relation to Podgrade, is it correct when it is noted here in the report that it states: "In Podgrade there was 1.760 old men, women, and children"?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: "The houses in the area filled were the minimum of 30 occupants each. Conditions are poor but there is sufficient food. There are indications that the HVO soldiers come into the area at night and rape the women they wish. All the men between 16 and 60 are gone. They," meaning the Muslims, I presume, "are very frightened concerning their future." That what you learned in Podgrade?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's what I learned there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did you know where did you make inquiries as to where the men had been moved, the men between 16 and 60?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: These men had been moved, in our opinion, or at least part of them to the POW camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: A POW camp where?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Do you know of -- how many had been moved on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No. When we visited it, it was -- the number of POWs in that camp was lower down that school. It was a school, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: According to your report you mention 167. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And you also --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Okay. That's up here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And you also received information that some other men had been moved to Capljina and Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Do you know under whose orders they had been moved?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did you make any inquiries afterwards?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Well, if you could turn to Exhibit 9621. On the 20th of August did you visit the village of Duge?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: On the 20th of August did you visit the village of Duge?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And 9621 is this your daily report of 20th of August?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, this is my daily report.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Authored by you and Mr. Hauenstein who appears to have returned?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And is it correct what is stated in paragraph 4 that you visited the Muslim community in Duge and you found the identical conditions as we found in Podgrade yesterday?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Next paragraph states that the third location, Lapsunj, was not visited. "The HVO stated they would not allow V2 access until such time as they provided a report of the Croat villages surrounding the area of Bugojno." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did you make inquiries as to what was intended for the Muslims who were in these three locations?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: What was intended?

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Okay. We did not -- we spoke about these things with the mayor, with the imam, but I shouldn't call it inquiries.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's too much for our questioning, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did anybody tell you that the movement of the Muslims to these three locations was merely a temporary movement and that they would be allowed to go back to their homes in Prozor?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Most of the time when we talked with several people about these kind of subjects it was always temporary, because there would always be a time after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: But I'm not talking about after the war. I'm talking within a couple of weeks of that time.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No. At that time no one want to bring back these people to their own houses where they came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Was there any --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: And, of course, the matter of ethnical cleansing, but they never told us that their object was ethnical cleansing. We could only guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Would it have been possible for the Muslims who were held in these three locations to return to their houses? Were they free and vacant?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No, not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Can you tell us why they weren't free and vacant?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Because of the patrol of military police and HVO, I think, as these Muslims told us when we visited Podgrade and Duge, because the guards who were on the roads to Podgrade. And all these things were telling us that they were a kind of imprisoned. They could freely move --

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did you ever --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: -- in that area of Podgrade and Duge but not outside that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: On this issue of whether they could go back to their homes or not, do you remember ever mentioning to the ICTY when you gave your statement that -- that Croat families had moved into houses there?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That Croat families -- Croat families. Okay. Yes. Croat families, I witnessed by myself, went into the houses later on in Podgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: In Podgrade?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I do not know the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Staying on this subject of the Muslims of Prozor, is it correct that you stated to the ICTY -- at page 11, that you spoke to the imam around this time and he had heard a rumour that the HVO had been moving Muslims from Podgrade to another town?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: If we could turn to Exhibit 4598, please.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: The 28th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: This is your report of the 28th of August, and is this authored by you and Mr. Hauenstein?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And if you turn to paragraph 2 at the top of the page, is it correct that you visited to the imam and that he provided what you described as "some additional disturbing news." The HVO have been moving Muslims from Podgrade throughout the day.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: From the Humanitarian Activity paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Top of page 2 on my copy. It's one, two, three -- it's the fourth paragraph under Humanitarian Activity.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Oh, the fourth.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Oh, page 2.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And the number of Muslims mentioned was 1.760.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Sixty, yes. Even more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: On learning this information did you go to the location where the Muslims were -- were held to see whether or not you could confirm it?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No, we didn't. To the new location?

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: When you learnt -- when you learned the Muslims had been moved --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: -- did you make any efforts to confirm this fact?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did you visit the location where they had been held?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes. We went to Podgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: And at a certain moment I don't know when but we saw the moving of these people. They were gathered into a truck to be brought to another place.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: And we saw empty Podgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And could you tell us who was -- who was in charge of this move in terms of the authorities? Who was handling the move?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: As far as I can recall now, I think the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did this development give you any cause for concern?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, of course, because it's -- it could be ethnical cleansing.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And were you able to find out from either the military authorities or the civilian authorities such as the mayor as to what was happening?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes. This was confirmed by several people.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: When you say several people, who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: The mayor, the -- Siljeg --

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: -- priest. All were in the end well-known of the fact that these -- these Muslim people were expelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did you in fact meet with Colonel Siljeg on the 1st of September, 1993, to discuss the issue?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I do not exactly know the date, but we discussed this issue with Siljeg, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: If you could turn to 9636. Again if you could just confirm that this is your daily report and authored by you?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: The 1st of September, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And if you turn to paragraph 4, Humanitarian Activity. We see that there's a notation that "the HVO representative of Prozor Colonel Siljeg confirm the expelling of 2.000 plus Muslims to Muslim territory near Konjic and Jablanica. They are moved on a voluntary basis. The military police is responsible for this action and they are acting independent." Is that what you were told by Colonel Siljeg?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And just in terms of the language used in this paragraph, you say: "The hope representative Colonel Siljeg confirm the expelling of the 2.000 plus to Muslim territory and says they were moved on a voluntary basis." I think you can see the contradiction there in terms. Did Colonel Siljeg use the word "expelling," or is that your word?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Colonel Siljeg was talking Croat, of course, and we always spoke through an interpreter, and I think it's possible that the word "expelling" is from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. And was this your belief, that they had been expelled?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did you make any inquiries to try and find out whether it had been a voluntary movement and confirm what Colonel Siljeg had told you?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: It was obvious -- it was obvious for me that it was not on a voluntary basis because of the fact that we visited Podgrade and Duge where we talked to these people, and these Muslim people who we talked to had a different opinion, and they were not saying that they were there in Podgrade and Duge on a voluntary basis and that they wanted left -- leave, that they wanted to leave Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: So it was your opinion that this was an expulsion?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did you follow up on what had actually happened to these people who were expelled? This was a large group of people, 2.000 plus Muslims. Did you make any inquiries as to what had become of them?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Well, sometimes we -- we asked for that and if anyone knows something about them. The only thing I've heard later is how they had to walk the last few metres to Muslim territory, and there should be shooting as well for -- on some occasion and some were killed. But that could not be confirm. That's what I heard on an occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And do you remember, did you hear who was shot at them -- who shot at them? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did you make any effort to contact the authorities in the ABiH area they were moved to?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No. These kind of -- because it was another material, these kind of questions should be made by RC Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Do you know how many people were shot that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Just a few we heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: So this it brought you up to the first week in September. I think you've mentioned earlier that during various dates in September that you saw the use of forced labour, and did it come about that in the middle of September you moved from one location to another and you moved from Gornji Vakuf to Tomislavgrad?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I moved to Tomislavgrad, yes, the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And who was -- who was the monitor that took over from you when you left?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Dave MacIver, the Canadian.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I believe that's it, Your Honours. I don't have any further questions. There were quite a number of exhibits in the booklet, but we made a decision that, given the fact that some items were outside the indictment, we were not going to put these. So I don't have any further questions. There is one correction that I would like to make. At the very outset when I was asking the witness if he remembered having giving a statement to the ICTY, I believe I may have mentioned the 9th of April, 2002. That was the date of the statement. In fact, I should have said the 7th of May, 2002. I'd like to make that correction. And that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I think that it would be better to have our last break now so as to allow the Defence to prepare. It's five past 5.00. We will resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resume. We will now proceed to the cross-examination stage. Considering the questions put by the Prosecution, we believe that three hours is sufficient for the cross-examination. I'm now going to give the floor to the Defence. I'd like to remind you that General Praljak should be granted one hour out of these three hours, one hour to put his questions to the witness. Let me now give the floor to the one who is going to start. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. I don't have any of my own documents, but I shall be using just two documents that you have in the Prosecution binder. And would you find document P 03263 to start off with. And may we have that document on e-court. It is P 03273. And we'll take a look at that together. It is a report, Gornji Vakuf, for the 7th of July, 1993. And I'd like us to look at point 4, Humanitarian Activities. And in point 4 under humanitarian activity it says as following: "The team visited the imam of Prozor today. He was extremely frightened and told us that almost all Muslim men between 16 and 60 have been arrested by the HVO. He would also like to see the entire Muslim population moved to a Muslim controlled area." Tell me now, please, did you know about these wishes expressed by the imam that the Muslims be moved to an area controlled by the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes. No, because it's not -- it's a report from the 7th of July, yes. I did not know of.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: I know that this report was written before you arrived in the Gornji Vakuf area, but unless I'm wrong, I think you told us earlier on that you knew what the situation was like before and that you were informed of the reports that had been written. So that's why I asked you. If you don't know, that's fine. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, please, do you know under whose control Jablanica and Konjic were in September 1993 and the end of August 1993? Who controlled those two towns?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No. I must guess.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: I'd like to go back to the last document you were looking at before the break, and it is P 09636.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: 9636. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: I am going to focus on point 4 and draw your attention to that paragraph, which was the one the Prosecutor asked you to look at as well. It refers to the deportation of 2.000 Muslims to the territory of Konjic and Jablanica. The Prosecutor, after focusing on that paragraph, asked you a question. He asked you whether you agreed with the statement made by Mr. Siljeg whereby the Muslims would go voluntarily, and you said you didn't agree with that, and that was on page 72 of the transcript, because the Muslims from Podgrade and Lapsunj told you that they were not moved to Podgrade and Lapsunj of their own free will, voluntarily. However, from this document we can see that it wasn't the fact that the Muslims were moved from Lapsunj and Podgrade but from Jablanica and Konjic. And from that I deduce that this movement to Jablanica and Konjic was not something that you had discussed. You had discussed their moving to Podgrade and Lapsunj. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I agree with you so far.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: In your statement, which you said you signed and is one of the documents, on page 11, that's in both in the Croatian and in the English version, in Croatian it is the last paragraph, in English it is the first paragraph, you describe the situation and say the following: "On the 28th of August, 1993, we talked to the imam, and he told us that he had heard rumours that the HVO was moving the Muslims from Podgrade to Rama, and he said that the same thing was happening in Duge and in Lapsunj as well. We drove to the entrance to Podgrade, and we saw a large truck parked next to the ramp. We stopped the car, went up to the truck and saw that it was full of women, children, and elderly Muslims. It was a green military truck, and I can't say whether it belonged to the military police or to the HVO because there was no difference in the vehicles those two sides used. I don't remember who was driving the truck." Do you remember saying that or words to that effect?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: From that I deduce that you do not know who did this moving of persons, whether it was the military police and whether it was voluntary or not. You don't know who actually carried it out.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Last week here in the courtroom -- you don't need that document any more, so you can forget about the binder. As I was saying, last week in the courtroom we heard Mr. Philip Watkins. I assume you know who Mr. Watkins is. Is that right? Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Watkins answered questions linked to the isolation of the Muslim population in the areas of Podgrade, Lapsunj, and Duge municipality, the subject you talked about today. And for the record, this was recorded on the pages of the transcript 19124, 19127, 19129, and 19130. During that examination or when asked, he said that a the isolation of the Muslim populous occurred after two massacres of the Croatian population, one of which was in the village of Uzdol, and that in his opinion it wasn't unreasonable to place the Muslim population, including the imam, in isolation for their own safety, in order to avoid retaliation or revenge being taken against them. Would you agree with that observation made by Mr. Watkins?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I would not agree because of the fact that Uzdol happened on the 15th of September and the expelling was before that date.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, tell me, please, today we heard you say, and we've heard this earlier on, this is something that Mr. Hauenstein on the 3rd of October 2006 told us about when he was testifying here, as did Mr. Watkins, too, they spoke about this situation with the imam, and that the military police would have prevented you from talking to him, from contacting him, and everybody said what you told us here this afternoon as well, and that is that as a rule when the military police prevented you from having contacts, after that you yourself would contact the individual, whether it was Mr. Siljeg or someone else, it depended, from the operative zone or the brigade, and that after that you would be allowed access. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Well, it -- I agree for -- I'm sure for one -- I know one case. I'm well aware of such -- such a case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, there's something that I don't find logical here. You told us that Mr. Siljeg did not have control over the military police. How, then, do you explain this situation? If they didn't allow you to contact the imam and then you contacted Mr. Siljeg or some other person from the brigade, and after that you were given permission to contact the imam. From this I make the logical conclusion that the military police nonetheless obeyed Mr. Siljeg.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Well, it's possible that they are obeying Mr. Siljeg. It's also possible that they negotiated about that. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: When Mr. Hauenstein was examined here, he spoke about the military structure as he knew it on the territory of Prozor and Vakuf, and this was recorded on the pages of the transcript 7836 and 7843. He said on that occasion that in Prozor the situation was such that there was the military police and that its commander was superior to it. I'm paraphrasing this. And up above its commander was the commander of the operative zone. He was the superior to them. Which means he told us something different than what you told us here this afternoon. Is it possible that Mr. Hauenstein was better informed about the situation than you because he spent much longer there, as far as I remember. He spent much longer on the ground. You were there for under two months yourself.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Well, I think we were both informed well. He stayed there for six months in that area. Hauenstein, I mean. Well, in my advantage, as you can call it -- as you may call it that way, is that I stayed in that area during the clashes, and on some events which were treated today he wasn't there. But I think for the preparation to the 18th of July where the war started in Bugojno between the Muslims and the Croats, he was better informed than me, because I wasn't there before that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, and I'd like to go back to your statement now, in the Croatian version it is on page 11, and in English it is on page 10, paragraph 3, and in it you say the following. You describe the 20th of August, 1993, and your tour of Duge, and somewhere in the middle of the paragraph you say: "We reported that there were regular police patrols in the area. It must have been the military police, because they were the only police force in the area at that time. They told us about these patrols. However, we did not see them." Do you remember that portion of your statement, having said that? Just give me a yes or no answer, please.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hauenstein, when he was here on the 3rd of October, and this was recorded on page 7863 of the transcript, lines 10 to 12, said that he had contacts with the civilian police in Prozor. Now, I am interested in knowing the following: Is it possible that only you did not know that the civilian police existed, whereas it did exist at that time but you did not have knowledge of that, since Mr. Hauenstein had meetings with that police force? At least that's what he says.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: It's my turn now?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Well, I've been -- I have been with -- I had meetings with the military police in Prozor as well together with Mr. Hauenstein, so I do not understand this question that I should not know of the existence of the military police in Prozor. I --

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: No. I asked you about the civilian police. He said that he met with the civilian police. Not the military police, the ordinary civilian police force?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: The ordinary civilian police. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. I'm not aware of that. It's strange -- it's strange for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, the Defence counsel is asking you whether you met with the civilian police. Your answer was that as far as you were concerned, there was only military, military police. Whilst looking at the documents earlier on, I noticed that in one of the documents it is stated that you went to Bugojno and that there at 1400 hours you met with the civilian police. You explained that there was lunch from noon to 2.00, and that 2.00 p.m. you met with the civilian police. In other words, there was a civilian police. It existed in Bugojno. Then how come the -- how do you explain there was no military -- or civilian police in Prozor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't explain. It's correct that we talked several times with the civilian police in Bugojno, and in my point of view the police which I met in Prozor was military police. That's the only thing I can say about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you have any information, specific information -- or, rather, do you know how many members of the military police had in Prozor? How many military policemen were there in Prozor?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No. The total amount I do not know. The only amount I know of is which I have seen at the house of the military police in Prozor, which were, approximate, five. More I haven't seen together.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you know whether and how many -- any military policemen were killed or died in Prozor and, if so, how many?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know whether they had a crime department and if they conducted any investigations into crimes committed? Do you know that they did this and, if so, how many investigations they undertook and things like that?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No. I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether they had a traffic department and what the traffic department did, if they had one?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Can I then conclude that your assessment that they didn't do their job properly was based on the fact that in your opinion they were uneducated people with -- who behaved badly? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: I have just one more brief question and that would conclude my cross-examination, and it is this: Tell me, please, and this is something that Mr. Hauenstein talked about and I'm going to ask you, the sexual abuse situations in the hotels, the Muslim women when they were isolated in the villages, Mr. Hauenstein told us that the situation was as follows: That at night from the forest, from some forest paths, various people would come in, forcefully abduct the women and take it out on them. Did you gain that impression? That was something that Mr. Hauenstein told us about.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: You are talking about Croat woman -- no, Muslim woman? When they were isolated in the villages. Okay. In Podgrade you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes, for example, Podgrade.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Hauenstein told us that the situation was as follows: That at night -- yes. From the forest path various people would come in, yes. That's the same I stated.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: And that that occurred at night mostly. That's what Mr. Hauenstein told us, too, that this happened during the night.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Well, these happenings were told us by the Muslim people in Podgrade and Duge, and we didn't witness these facts personally. So it was declarations from the people in Podgrade and Duge.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that and that's quite clear. But I asked you whether this happened during the night, because that's how Mr. Hauenstein described these events, that they happened during the night. And we have it on page 7856 of the transcript up to 7858.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's what I said, the people in Podgrade and Duge.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Now, to me it would be logical that if somebody jumps out of the woods at night in order to do their dirty business that they would be fully conscious that they ought not to be doing that and that they would be in hiding so as not to be discovered, because if that was something that was allowed, then they would have no need of doing it at night, coming out of the woods. He would do it in broad daylight in a public place. Am I right in that logic?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I think daylight or night-light is not the issue, but okay. It's not logic for me. The only logical thing for me is that it was not allowed. I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: We have already heard from you that over there during the day there were patrols patrolling the area, and those who attacked could have known that there were patrols. So would it be logical that they waited for night-time, under cover of darkness, so that the patrols wouldn't see them and that then they could carry out what they intended to?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I think all kind of thing are possible. I don't know what they -- how they did it, and the only thing I can say what I heard from the people in Podgrade and Duge, and that's in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. This concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Next counsel. Mr. Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have no questions for this witness, and we cede our time to the other Defence teams. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Ibrisimovic. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon Mr. President. I do have some questions for the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My name is Michael Karnavas. Together with Suzana Tomanovic we represented Mr. Jadranko Prlic. You're shaking your head. Now, let me ask you one question. Did thinks name come up when you were in theatre?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did anyone say they had to consult with Dr. Prlic at any time?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I need to slow down a little bit. Help me out here. You arrived in theatre sometime in July; correct?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Prior to arriving you had a two- or three-week orientation, training, what have you; correct?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you had been in the military for a long time so more or less you -- as I understand it, you were in logistics?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when you got in theatre it was slightly different than you had expected.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fact, when you got there a real war was going on.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it was probably the first time in your career that there you were as a trained military officer --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, hold on.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As a military officer in a white uniform, unarmed, being in the middle of a real war.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: In a white uniform, yes. But in a green uniform, I've seen war before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You've seen war before, but also you had access to weapons that you could fire back at.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And my whole point was: There you were, exposed. You were there as a monitor just to -- to observe.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, in reading your statement, I notice that you had notes that you took contemporaneously as you were in -- in theatre; right?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you consulted your notes as you were preparing for your statement.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Because you wanted to be -- to be as accurate as you possibly could be.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, on page 5 of your statement, and I see that the statement that I'm referring to was taken on March 20th and on April 9th, 2002. So I take it they met with you twice. And on page 5 there was something that sort of caught my attention, and what I'm referring to is the one part where you say that: "I was --"

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Sorry, just to interrupt you. Just a point of information. I think you may be referring to the ABiH statement and not the HVO statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, be that as it may it's's a staple the officer gave and I'm going to ask about something. May I ask the question and then you can object all you want?

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I thought you were referring to the exhibit that was presented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You say in your statement: "I was considerably less naive about the intentions of the Muslim leadership by the time I left Bugojno." Now, that's on page 5 of that particular statement, and it's in reference to apparently the Muslim leadership had indicated to you that they were investigating allegations that had been raised by the Croats, by Father Janko, with respect to certain crimes. Now, my question is this: When you say, "I was less naive," and I hate to put you on the spot, but --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Oh, no. No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- you would be able to tell us because you chose those words.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So, how naive were you, or what exactly were you told --

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: What I was saying there that's the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No. What were you told when you got there, because obviously they must have told you something before coming into theatre or was this sort of innocent naivete about the good intentions of mankind, and there you were in the war only to find out that at least some people or a group of people were less than honourable or less than honest in whatever they said and did?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Well, and -- let me put it another way. It's hard in war, that's what I experienced myself, to stay as honourable as it should be, you know? It's hard working to believe in all the concepts mankind has.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: You know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I read your two statements. I read your testimony it. The first time, I believe, you testified in the Kordic case; you were a Defence witness. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then the second time you were a Prosecution witness in the Hadzihasanovic case.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So on both occasions -- on the one occasion you were initially questioned by the Defence. On the second occasion you were questioned by the Prosecution essentially about things that you saw and did in theatre while you were with ECMM; correct?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it you were under oath as you are today and whatever you said then and say today is to the best of your knowledge true, honest, and complete.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, in one of your statements you indicated that when you got there it was the Muslim army that was the attacking army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that they were on the winning side.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: In the area of Bugojno, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where you were.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, when you say they were on the winning side, what exactly did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: In military terms that they gained ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So I take it their objective was to gain ground?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I think not the only objective. As military people, the objective should be made on a political level, and the military people are just an arm of the politicians, and I'm not totally aware of the aims of the politicians in Bosnia, so that's a problem. I could only monitor, what my job was, that the Muslims, the ABiH, was gaining ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Taking territory?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Taking territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And is it fair to say that usually in a war that's one of the objectives?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That's one of -- could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could be. Right. Exactly. But in this particular war, at least what you were able to see and glean from and conclude was that the Muslim army was the attacking army where you were, that they were on the winning side. I take it that on the other side you had the Croat army; right? You know, the HVO.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's what I mean. And they were on the losing side.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: At that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At that time. So they were retreating or losing territory?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In between -- sandwiched in between the two armies, I would imagine -- because this was not done in some open field where the boys just got together to play, in between you had civilians. You had villages.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And that's where you found -- that's where you had unarmed civilian population.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so they were caught in the middle, more or less?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: In a lot of cases, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In a lot of cases. Would it be fair to say that those people that are caught in the middle between two fighting armies would at least be frightened?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would want to leave?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we're going to get there step-by-step.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Because I understand that at least one organisation, UNHCR, their mission, their belief, you know, was to keep the population there in the middle of the war.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Oh, yes, from the UNHCR. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so at least that's what it would appear, that in order to move anybody out of a particular place would constitute "ethnic cleansing."

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.
